canonical_name: Strong maximum principle for harmonic functions
canonical_statement: Let Omega be a nonempty connected open subset of R^n and let u : Omega -> R be harmonic. If u attains a maximum at a point of Omega, then u is constant on Omega.
domain_and_universes: Provisional classical Euclidean formulation: n : Nat; Omega : Set (EuclideanSpace Real (Fin n)); u : Omega -> Real. The statement phase must choose the actual mathlib harmonicity API.
hypotheses: forall x : Omega, u x <= u x0
conclusion: forall x : Omega, u x = u x0

scope_decisions.included: Real-valued classical harmonic functions on a connected open Euclidean domain; an attained interior global maximum; constancy on the whole domain.
scope_decisions.equivalent_candidate: An interior local maximum implies constancy, after restricting to a neighborhood and using propagation/connectedness; this requires a checked transport.
scope_decisions.excluded: Weak boundary maximum principles, subharmonic functions, general uniformly elliptic operators, manifolds, discrete harmonic functions, vector-valued functions, and minimum versions unless connected by a checked negation transport.

degenerate_cases: Nonemptiness is explicit. Dimension zero and singleton-domain behavior must be mutation-tested rather than silently discarded. Disconnected domains are excluded because an extremum on one component does not force global constancy.
